From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit (Acme Retail)

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap from our side so we have alignment on pain, success criteria, and next steps. Please reply with any corrections.

Pain points / drivers
- Current inference variability during peak campaign windows causing latency spikes and 5–15% failed requests.
- Need for data isolation and contractual guarantees for customer data (security/compliance).
- Cost predictability for seasonal traffic (marketing-driven bursts).

Current stack
- Inference runs on a mix of managed endpoints (cloud vendor) + some self-hosted GPUs for high-sensitivity workloads.
- Model: in-house fine-tuned Llama-2-70B variant, using FP16; sequence lengths avg ~512, tail to 1024.
- Traffic profile: baseline ~80 requests/sec (avg), peak sustained ~300–400 req/sec during campaigns; short bursts up to ~700 req/sec for 3–10 minutes once/month. (You mentioned these numbers roughly — see attached acme-malp-usage.csv for sample week)

Success criteria for Dedicated fit
- Predictable TPS/latency: 99th percentile latency < 300ms for interactive flows at target throughput; SLO-backed support.
- Isolation: dedicated GPU pools and tenancy isolation for regulated workloads.
- Autoscale/burst: ability to sustain short bursts (3–10 minutes) without cold-starts while keeping unit cost within budget envelope.
- Operational: monitoring, token-level cost breakdowns, and canary rollout support for model versions.

Proposed next steps
1) Marcus (SE) to run a capacity / cost estimate based on your sample usage and model shape (Marcus will follow up with a short worksheet).
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive (60m) next week to review traffic patterns, autoscaling policy, and isolation requirements.
3) Marissa to share an initial Dedicated quote and contract milestones.

Attachments: acme-malp-usage.csv (sample traffic export)

If this looks right, can you confirm the peak burst numbers and preferred time for the deep-dive (I suggested Tue/Wed next week in our calendar).

Thanks — looking forward to working through fit.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa —

Appreciate the clear recap. That matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:
- Peak sustained numbers: our traffic team confirms sustained peaks typically around 350 req/sec for campaign windows (10–12 hours), but there are brief promotional blasts (web push + email) that spike to ~700 req/sec for ~5–8 minutes.
- Latency requirement: 99th < 400ms is our hard requirement for customer-facing flows; batch/async backfills can be higher.
- Isolation/compliance: we will need dedicated tenancy for the production workload and SOC2 evidence for onboarding.

Ravi (cc) will own procurement and contract terms; he’ll want the initial quote and any model of overage/burst charges.

We’d like the technical deep-dive on Wednesday 2026-03-31 between 10:00–11:00 PT if that works for your team.

- For Llama-2-70B at fp16 with sequence mix (avg 512, tail 1024), estimate: 6x A100-like GPUs for sustained 350 TPS at p99 ~360ms with batching and KV cache.
